assumptions: Pure preselection |psi_i> and rank-one pure postselection |psi_f>, represented at the same measurement time in a common picture; any intervening free evolution is absorbed into those states.
The normalized states have nonzero overlap <psi_f|psi_i>. The displayed quotient is undefined at zero overlap.
This audited scope uses a Hermitian observable A on a finite-dimensional system. Mixed-state preselection and general postselection effects require a separately stated generalization.
variables: A: system observable; |psi_i>: preselected state; <psi_f|: bra associated with the selected final state.
A_w: generally complex transition-amplitude ratio, not an eigenvalue required of an individual ideal projective measurement.
patch.units: A_w has the same physical units as A; the state overlap is dimensionless. A Pauli component sigma_z is dimensionless, whereas S_z=(hbar/2)sigma_z and its weak value have units of angular momentum.
patch.regime: An exact definition for the declared pure-state, nonzero-overlap domain. Its leading-order weak-measurement interpretation additionally requires a controlled system-meter expansion after postselection. Near-orthogonal postselection can make A_w large but makes the weak-coupling limit nonuniform; small bare coupling alone does not justify extrapolation. A_w may be complex or, when real, outside A's eigenvalue interval, without changing the eigenvalues available to a strong projective measurement. No universal metrological advantage is asserted.
